official.description_text:
Doctoral student in Feminist AI Addressing Gender-Based Violence
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Information and Communication Technology
We at the Department of Computing and Learning Systems (CLS) are seeking a PhD student to join a fully funded research project on Feminist AI Addressing Gender-Based Violence. The project aims to develop novel AI methods that make online gender-based violence visible by detecting not only explicit abuse but also the structural silences and omissions that shape digital narratives. By combining advances in large language models (LLMs), natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning (ML), the project explores how AI can identify missing voices, hidden patterns, and gaps in institutional accountability to support more responsible, transparent, and socially aware AI systems.
The successful candidate will develop novel ML models and evaluation methods, construct large-scale datasets and knowledge graphs, collaborate with feminist organizations and civil society partners, and publish research in leading AI venues. The project offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research at the intersection of AI, equity, and justice.
You will join an interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment that values scientific excellence, intellectual curiosity, diversity, and research with real societal impact. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful, and supportive research culture where everyone can thrive. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen research and innovation, and we particularly encourage applications from groups that are underrepresented in AI and computer science.
Supervision:
Associate professor Amir Hossein Payberah
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree:
Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement

Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled

ai.summary: KTH doctoral position developing machine learning and NLP methods to detect gender-based violence in online spaces, combining LLMs, NLP, and ML with collaboration from feminist organizations and civil society partners.

thematic_fit.rationale: The researcher's core identity centers on human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, and collaborative learning—domains entirely disconnected from gender-based violence detection, online content moderation, or social justice applications of AI. While both involve HCI broadly, the thematic distance is substantial.

methodological_fit.rationale: The position is pure ML/NLP algorithm development (LLMs, knowledge graphs, dataset construction, evaluation metrics). The researcher has intermediate quantitative-research and user-studies skills but no background in NLP, LLMs, or the mathematical/statistical foundations required for this work. User studies in the researcher's domain validate immersive experiences; they do not transfer to ML model evaluation.

growth_value.rationale: A significant pivot from immersive systems to pure ML/NLP would add algorithmic depth but would not advance the researcher's stated growth trajectory toward human-centred immersive research. It would consume PhD years on an unrelated domain.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a leading institution with strong AI credentials and funding stability. The interdisciplinary framing and societal impact alignment are intellectually serious. However, the supervisor (Amir Hossein Payberah) works in ML systems, not HCI—no path to the researcher's target identity or future collaborations in immersive systems research.

eligibility_flags: Researcher has beginner Python; role requires proficiency for substantial model development and dataset construction.
No background in NLP, LLMs, or knowledge graph construction.
Admission requires demonstrated excellence in theoretical analysis of stochastic phenomena; researcher has not demonstrated this.
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch would make the first 6–12 months remedial rather than research-productive.
No existing supervisor relationship or research group fit; starting from zero in a specialized ML area.
Investing PhD time here delays entry into target immersive systems research community.
